items.caption:
Your brain stays on guard in a new bed.
In a 35-person Brown University study, a network in the left half of the brain slept lighter on night one and woke people faster to odd sounds. By night two, the difference was gone.

items.caption:
Why do your worries feel bigger after midnight?
One sleep researcher says 3 to 4 a.m. is a body-clock turning point when we're at our lowest ebb and alone in the dark. A 2022 hypothesis says night tilts mood negative. Brief wake-ups are normal.

items.caption:
Falling asleep in under 5 minutes is not a flex.
Normal sleep latency is around 10 to 20 minutes. Dropping off almost instantly, night after night, can be a sign of sleep debt rather than great sleep. If it's every night and you're tired by day, talk to a doctor.
